proof.criterion: A1/R2: a Dispatch server with no DISPATCH_SIGNIN_* setting and DISPATCH_IDENTITY unset boots, serves the agent-token API, and answers GET /auth/start with a refusal that says browser sign-in is off.
proof.surface: The real envoy-dispatch binary built from this head, run as a process against a real Postgres (Debian PostgreSQL 17.11 with pgvector at 127.0.0.1:5433) on a database of my own, driven over HTTP with curl. The second boot of this row carries DISPATCH_SERVER_URL='http://example-dispatch.dispatch.svc.cluster.local:8766', the exact string the component renders for a sandbox, so the component's output and the binary's acceptance of it are proven to meet.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && go build -o $TMPDIR/tester-dispatch ./cmd/dispatch; psql .../postgres -c 'create database tester_nosignin'; env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=$TMPDIR TMPDIR=$TMPDIR DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/tester_nosignin?sslmode=disable' DISPATCH_AGENT_TOKEN=tester-agent-token DISPATCH_LISTEN_HOST=127.0.0.1 DISPATCH_PORT=18790 DISPATCH_SERVER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18790 $TMPDIR/tester-dispatch (no DISPATCH_SIGNIN_* and no DISPATCH_IDENTITY at all), then curl against /healthz, /api/v1/whoami, /auth/start, /auth/callback?code=x&state=y, /auth/callback with no parameters, /auth/_dev/signin, /api/v1/projects and /api/v1/inbox; then the same boot again on port 18792 and database tester_clusterurl with DISPATCH_SERVER_URL='http://example-dispatch.dispatch.svc.cluster.local:8766'.
proof.observed: Both boots migrated and logged 'dispatch: listening'. /healthz answered 200 with "signin":null. GET /api/v1/whoami with the agent token answered 200 {"kind":"agent","owner":null,"service":null}. GET /auth/start answered 503 {"code":"SIGNIN_UNCONFIGURED",...}. GET /auth/callback, with and without parameters, answered the same 503 SIGNIN_UNCONFIGURED rather than panicking on a nil sign-in flow. GET /auth/_dev/signin answered 404 NOT_FOUND, so no dev sign-in route is mounted. The agent-token API serves writes as well as reads: POST /api/v1/projects with {"actor":{"kind":"session",...}} answered 201 and the project then appears in GET /api/v1/projects. Every one of these held identically on the second boot, the one carrying the in-cluster DISPATCH_SERVER_URL the component renders, so a sandbox pod's own server URL is a value this binary accepts.
proof.negativeControl: Five refusals, each driven at the same head. (1) A partial sign-in set: the same boot with DISPATCH_SIGNIN_DOMAIN=example.com alone (the implementer used DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID, so this is a different input) exited with 'Google sign-in needs DISPATCH_SIGNIN_ISSUER, DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID, DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET and one of DISPATCH_SIGNIN_GROUP or DISPATCH_SIGNIN_DOMAIN: DISPATCH_SIGNIN_DOMAIN set, DISPATCH_SIGNIN_ISSUER, DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID, DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET missing', so half a sign-in still refuses the boot. (2) The party it must refuse: GET /api/v1/whoami with Bearer nope answered 401 {"code":"UNAUTHORIZED"}. (3) With no Authorization header at all it answered 401 {"code":"NO_IDENTITY"}, so removing requireCookieSignIn opened no anonymous door. (4) With a forged 'Cookie: dsession=forged.value.here' it answered 401 NO_IDENTITY, and with 'X-Dispatch-User: someone@example.com' 401 NO_IDENTITY, so neither a made-up session cookie nor a header names a person on a cookie-identity server with sign-in off. (5) A human-only route, GET /api/v1/inbox, answered the agent token 403 {"code":"HUMAN_ONLY"}. No response of any probe carried a Set-Cookie header.

proof.criterion: A1/R2 second half: production's settings boot as today — the same binary with the whole sign-in set still signs people in.
proof.surface: The same real envoy-dispatch binary from this head on the same Postgres, on a database and port of its own.
proof.command: env -i ... DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5433/tester_signin?sslmode=disable' DISPATCH_PORT=18791 DISPATCH_SERVER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18791 DISPATCH_SIGNIN_ISSUER=https://accounts.google.com DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_ID=example-client-id DISPATCH_SIGNIN_CLIENT_SECRET=example-client-secret DISPATCH_SIGNIN_DOMAIN=example.com $TMPDIR/tester-dispatch, then curl /healthz and /auth/start.
proof.observed: The boot logged 'dispatch: signing people in with Google for a Workspace domain issuer=https://accounts.google.com client_id=example-client-id domain=example.com'. /healthz answered "signin":true. GET /auth/start answered 302 to https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?...&client_id=example-client-id&hd=example.com&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A18791%2Fauth%2Fcallback&response_type=code&scope=openid+email+profile&state=..., which is the production sign-in flow unchanged. The agent token still answers 200 on this server too.
proof.negativeControl: The differential is the control: the same binary with the sign-in settings removed answers "signin":null and 503 SIGNIN_UNCONFIGURED at /auth/start (the row above), so the 302 here is the settings' doing and not a path that ignores them.

proof.observed: ok github.com/sjawhar/envoy/infra/gcp 54.635s — every sandbox test, the Construct case and the nine partial-group subtests pass. My leak scan found no sandbox property naming the front door or a sign-in variable. My reference walk found no dangling reference in the sandbox: every Secret and ConfigMap its objects name is one of the two the run declares. (Run against the default mode the same walk reports example-dispatch-tailnet mounting kube-root-ca.crt, the ConfigMap Kubernetes puts in every namespace, which is the walk finding references at all and is unchanged by this branch.) The combination decision D3 leaves allowed and no test drives — the whole tailnet group set with the sign-in group empty — resolves and renders: the front door and its serve ConfigMap are built, DISPATCH_SERVER_URL is https://example-dispatch.example-tailnet.ts.net, no app variable begins DISPATCH_SIGNIN_, and the <hostname>-dispatch Secret holds DATABASE_URL, DISPATCH_AGENT_TOKEN and DISPATCH_SIGNING_KEY alone, so the nil pulumi.StringInput the implementer's trickyParts warns about never reaches refuseDispatchSeedInSecret in that mode either.

None of these shapes resolves.

notesForTheArchitect: Decision D3 leaves one input combination allowed that nothing tests and that removes a refusal production had: the whole tailnet group set with the sign-in group empty. Before this change gcp.ResolveDispatch refused an empty signInClientId whatever the mode; now it resolves, and the component renders a tailnet Dispatch whose app carries no DISPATCH_SIGNIN_* variable, so every person is locked out while the agent API serves. I drove that combination and it renders coherently, so it is no defect and I wrote no red test for it. The risk it would otherwise carry is closed by the one consumer that exists: theorem-labs/agent-infra's dispatch/main.go reads signInClientId and signInDomain with cfg.Try and signInClientSecret with cfg.TrySecret and refuses the program when a key is missing (its refusals list), so the production stack cannot reach the combination by losing a config key. I report it because the reviewer should see it named rather than infer it.
